brief:
My GRIP arm's elbow has a hard stop, and when the controller overshoots, the forearm slams into it.
I want a TPU 95A pad, printed on my FDM printer (0.4 mm nozzle), to glue onto the stop. Worst case
the forearm arrives with about 1.2 kg of effective mass at 1 m/s, square onto the pad's top face.
The force on the stop has to stay under 220 N or the servo's gears are at risk, and the pad must not
squash more than 8 mm. It has a 30 x 30 mm footprint and can be at most 15 mm tall: put the stop face
at z = 0, the pad centred on x = y = 0 and going up from there. Give it flat solid faces about 1 mm
thick top and bottom, so it glues on and the forearm hits a surface rather than cell edges.
